The words

I'm but a stranger here,
Heav'n is my home;
Earth is a desert drear,
Heav'n is my home.
Danger and sorrow stand
round me on every hand;
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

What though the tempest rage,
Heav'n is my home;
Short is my pilgrimage,
Heav'n is my home;
Time's wild and wintry blast
soon shall be over past;
I shall reach home at last,
Heav'n is my home.

There at my Savior's side
Heav'n is my home;
I shall be glorified,
Heav'n is my home.
There are the good and blest,
those I loved most and best;
There, too, I soon shall rest,
Heav'n is my home.

Therefore I murmur not,
Heav'n is my home;
Whate'er my earthly lot,
Heav'n is my home;
And I shall surely stand
there at my Lord's right hand.
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum G and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (G).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by Thomas Rawson Taylor, first published in 1836. The tune, ST. EDMUND (SULLIVAN), is by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1872). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1836): Thomas Rawson Taylor (1807–1835)
  • Music (1872): Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900)

Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. EDMUND (SULLIVAN) by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900); words by Thomas Rawson Taylor (1807–1835). Questions about I'm but a Stranger Here

What is the doh of I'm but a Stranger Here?

In this version, in G major, doh is G. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does I'm but a Stranger Here start on?

It starts on d (G in G major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is I'm but a Stranger Here in the public domain?

Yes. Thomas Rawson Taylor died in 1835, Arthur Seymour Sullivan died in 1900; the words were first published in 1836 and the music in 1872. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
